name: Central Mfumte
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.quote: We have identified five surface tones in Mfumte: three level tones: high [á], mid [ā] and low [à]; and two contour tones, rising [ǎ] and falling [â]. ... As of this point in time, we have discovered many minimal tone pairs for words that contrast the level tones: high, mid and low with each other and we conclude that these three tones need to be clearly distinguished from each other.
new_statements.citation: Eyoh, Julius A. and Robert Hedinger. 2008. Mfumte orthography guide. Yaoundé: NACALCO. (SIL Language & Culture Archives 32291)

new_statements.rule_in_words: Central Mfumte (Lus) is described as a tone language with three contrastive level tones (H, M, L) plus rising and falling contours, tone carrying both lexical and grammatical (plural, hortative/imperative) contrasts; neither this guide nor McLean's 2014 sketch grammar says anything about word stress or accent, so no stress position can be stated from accessible sources.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. (Tone: rising tone mostly grammatical - noun plurals, hortatives/imperatives; falling tone concentrated on the prefix mâ- and second syllables of reduplicated roots, p. 9.)
new_statements.domain_note: Tone description refers to isolation (citation) forms: 'Our proposal is to write all Mfumte words as they occur in isolation' (p. 9). McLean 2014 p. 9 likewise uses surface tone only and adds a 'super high' surface tone in its conventions (p. 5). No statement at word or phrase level about stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Both held sources describe the variety of the village of Lus (Ndə'wuli'), which McLean 2014 explicitly calls 'Central Mfumte' (= Glottolog cent2312) and which Eyoh & Hedinger 2008 treat as the standard 'Mfumte' variety; both carry ISO nfu, which Glottolog now assigns to Southern Mfumte (mfum1238, Koffa etc.), so the ISO code alone would misfile them. Glottolog's own comment on cent2312 equates it with Ethnologue's 'Kwaja (kdz-NOCODE_Central-Mfumte)' entry.

sources.citation: Eyoh, Julius A. and Robert Hedinger. 2008. Mfumte orthography guide. Yaoundé: NACALCO. (SIL Language & Culture Archives 32291)
sources.quote: We have identified five surface tones in Mfumte: three level tones: high [á], mid [ā] and low [à]; and two contour tones, rising [ǎ] and falling [â]. ... As of this point in time, we have discovered many minimal tone pairs for words that contrast the level tones: high, mid and low with each other and we conclude that these three tones need to be clearly distinguished from each other.
sources.note: Nothing about stress or accent. Sec. 3 'Tones' pp. 8-10: five surface tones (high, mid, low level; rising, falling contour), many H/M/L minimal pairs, tone also marks noun plural and hortative/imperative; consonant/vowel phoneme charts pp. 2-8. Based on the Lus (standard) variety.

sources.note: Nothing. Morphosyntax sketch only; tone diacritic conventions (H, M, L, super-high, falling, rising) in the abbreviations p.5; sec. 1.5 p.9 'Surface tone markings are used and no formal attempt has been made to account for tonal alternation'; sec. 6 p.34 'the role of tone in Central Mfumte grammar remains to be fully researched'.
